new_statements.citation: Haan, Johnson Welem. 2001. The grammar of Adang: a Papuan language spoken on the island of Alor, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia. PhD dissertation, University of Sydney, xix+416 pp.
new_statements.check: reported on verification, not yet confirmed
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Not applicable: the item lists exactly one work (Haan 2001), which the compiler opened; there are no silent or not-opened works to spot-check. As an extra check I a full-text search for stress/accent the other on-disk hama1240 texts (Tondo 2012 JPK, Adhiti 2017, Adhiti 2020, Sanubarianto 2025) for tekanan/stress/aksen/penultima/suprasegmental: no hits, matching the earlier record. The Stokhof 1975 p. 47 page scan (list '19. KABOLA (HAMAP)') shows the prominence marks the compiler describes (e.g. n'afah, s'ana, m'aru, h'ala, n'ɔfi vs tar'ɔp, hab'ar, ham'uy, nad'ɛr, mah'il, tal'an, tur'al) and no rule statement.

sources.citation: Adhiti, Ida Ayu Iran. 2017. Pantulan (refleks) Proto Austronesia (PAN) ke protobahasa Kabola, protobahasa Hamap, dan protobahasa Klon di Pulau Alor, NTT. Kulturistik 1(1): 32-45. DOI 10.22225/kulturistik.1.1.215
sources.note: Segmental reflex correspondences only; no stress/tekanan.

sources.citation: Holton, Gary & Laura C. Robinson. 2017. The internal history of the Alor-Pantar language family. In Marian Klamer (ed.), The Alor-Pantar languages: history and typology, 2nd ed., 49-90. Berlin: Language Science Press (LangSci 157). Also ch. 1 (Klamer), ch. 3 (Schapper, Huber & van Engelenhoven), ch. 7 (Schapper & Klamer) which use Hamap data.
sources.note: p. 55, family level only: 'In most of the modern languages stress is on the penultimate syllable; however, stress may also be attracted to heavy syllables, as in Teiwa jiˈvar dog. In addition, stress may be phonemically contrastive in some languages, as in Western Pantar..'. Hamap forms in the volume (Robinson fieldnotes 2010; Baird fieldnotes 2003) carry no stress marks; nothing Hamap-specific.

sources.citation: Haan, Johnson Welem. 2001. The grammar of Adang: a Papuan language spoken on the island of Alor, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia. PhD dissertation, University of Sydney, xix+416 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Adang is Hamap's closest relative (Adang-Hamap-Kabola dialect chain); its stress statement would be the nearest first-hand rule and a check on the Stokhof pattern. Open copy exists but the host blocks our network.

sources.citation: Sanubarianto, Salimulloh Tegar. 2025. Kui, Hamap, and Kamang language kinship in Alor Regency: toward Proto-Alor-Pantar reconstruction. Southeast Asian Language and Literature Studies 2(2): 101-120. DOI 10.55981/salls.2025.13484
sources.note: Lexicostatistics and sound correspondences; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Adhiti, Ida Ayu Iran. 2020. Sinonimi bahasa Kabola dan bahasa Hamap di Pulau Alor, NTT: suatu kajian deskriptif analisis. Kulturistik 4(2): 60-68. DOI 10.22225/kulturistik.4.2.1896
sources.note: Lexical comparison Kabola/Hamap; phonemic transcription without stress marks; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Tondo, Fanny Henry. 2012. Bahasa minoritas Hamap dalam perkebunan jagung: tinjauan etnolinguistik. Jurnal Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan 18(2): 204-215. DOI 10.24832/jpnk.v18i2.82
sources.note: pp. 207-208 summarise Tondo 2006: 7 vowel + 15 consonant phonemes, long vowels i: e: a: o: u:, diphthongs ai/oi, 1-4 syllable word patterns (in, e, mul; asel, faur; afael, afutu; arilohing, nadarefang). No mention of stress/tekanan. Its reference list identifies the primary phonology chapter: Tondo 2006 in Katubi (ed.), LIPI Press.

sources.citation: LexiRumah 3 (Kaiping, Edwards & Klamer), forms for lect hama1240 (231 forms, source baird03 = Baird 2003 West Alor survey wordlist)
sources.note: IPA forms carry no stress marks; no stress information.

sources.citation: Stokhof, W. A. L. 1975. Preliminary notes on the Alor and Pantar languages (East Indonesia). Pacific Linguistics B-43. Canberra: ANU. vi+79 pp. (Glottolog 161717; the source the earlier scan named as unreachable)
sources.note: p. 2 defines ' as relative vowel prominence within a word and " as a lighter second peak; wordlist 19 'Kabola (Hamap)' p. 47 marks prominence on every polysyllable but states no rule. Marks fall on the penult in most open-final words and on the final in most closed-final words, with exceptions both ways.

tone.quote: Tataran fonologi berbicara seputar fonem. [...] Hal tersebut dapat dilihat pada pasangan kata /he/ ‘itu’ dan /ho/ ‘ini’, atau pasangan kata /a:la/ ‘padi’ dan /a:lo/ ‘dua’. [...] Dalam bahasa Hamap terdapat enam vokal dan lima belas konsonan. Di samping itu, ada pula vokal panjang dan diftong.
tone.locator: p. 110 (journal pagination), section III 'Sekilas tentang Mikrolinguistik Hamap'
tone.translation: The phonological level is about phonemes. [...] This can be seen in the word pair /he/ 'that' and /ho/ 'this', or the pair /a:la/ 'rice' and /a:lo/ 'two'. [...] Hamap has six vowels and fifteen consonants. In addition there are also long vowels and diphthongs.
